Algebra I · Lesson 3.4

Radicals and Simplification

Solve this lesson →All lessons
Problem
Every answer in 3.3 came out whole because every base was a perfect power. Neither 2451/22451/2 nor 51/251/2 is a whole number. But power of a product from 3.1 reads in both directions, so two half powers can merge into one. Combine 2451/2⋅51/22451/2⋅51/2 into a single power and enter its value.
Show a hint
  • The law that splits (ab)1/2(ab)1/2 into a1/2b1/2a1/2b1/2 also runs right to left. Two half powers of different bases can become one half power.
  • 245⋅5=1225245⋅5=1225. What number squares to 12251225?
Show the full solution
Merging the half powers gives 2451/2⋅51/2=(245⋅5)1/2=12251/22451/2⋅51/2=(245⋅5)1/2=12251/2, and 352=1225352=1225, so the value is 3535​. Two numbers that are not whole on their own multiplied to a number that is. This lesson runs on that move.

The product came out whole, but 2451/22451/2 on its own did not go away. It is a genuine number, somewhere between 1515 and 1616 since 152=225152=225 and 162=256162=256, and no whole number or fraction squares to exactly 245245. A number like that cannot be evaluated into anything simpler. It needs a way to be written.

Key idea
The radical sign. xx​ is x1/2x1/2, the same number written with a new symbol. The symbol is a radical sign, the number under it is the radicand, and xx​ is read as the square root of xx. Higher roots carry a small index, x3=x1/33x​=x1/3 is the cube root, xn=x1/nnx​=x1/n is the nnth root, and a radical with no index always means the square root. Since the number is the same, everything 3.3 settled still applies. xx​ names the nonnegative choice, and an even root of a negative radicand names no real number.
Problem
3.3 settled which roots accept a negative base, and the new symbol changes none of it. Exactly one of −1000−1000​ and −100033−1000​ names a real number. Enter its value.
Show a hint
  • An even root needs a nonnegative radicand. An odd root takes any sign.
  • What number cubed gives −1000−1000?
Show the full solution
(−10)3=(−10)(−10)(−10)=−1000(−10)3=(−10)(−10)(−10)=−1000, so −10003=−103−1000​=−10​. No real number squares to −1000−1000, since squares are never negative, so −1000−1000​ names nothing at all.

4141​ sits between 66 and 77, since 62=3662=36 and 72=4972=49, and no fraction squares to 4141. The symbol is still exact. The square of 4141​ is exactly 4141, while any decimal you could type squares to nearly 4141 and misses. So 4141​ is not an unfinished computation. It is the answer, and it stays written.

Key idea
The product rule for radicals. Power of a product from 3.1 gives (ab)1/2=a1/2b1/2(ab)1/2=a1/2b1/2, which in radical notation reads ab=a bab​=a​b​ for nonnegative aa and bb. Nothing new is being asserted, this is a 3.1 law restated in the new symbol. Like any equation it works in both directions. Left to right it splits one radical into two, and right to left it merges two radicals into one, which is exactly what the opening problem did before the rule had a name.
Problem
The rule claims 64⋅49=64⋅4964⋅49​=64​⋅49​. Test it the 1.4 way. The right side is quick. Confirm the left side agrees, then enter the shared value.
Show a hint
  • Work each side on its own. The claim is true only if the two values match.
  • 64⋅49=8⋅764​⋅49​=8⋅7. Square that product and compare it with 64⋅4964⋅49.
Show the full solution
64⋅49=8⋅7=5664​⋅49​=8⋅7=56, and 64⋅49=313664⋅49=3136 with 562=3136562=3136, so 3136=563136​=56 as well. Both sides land on 5656​.
Key idea
Simplified form. Splitting is the useful direction when the radicand is large. Back to 245245​ from the opening problem. Since 245=49⋅5245=49⋅5 and 4949 is a perfect square, 245=49 5=75.245​=49​5​=75​. The perfect-square factor left the radical as 77, and only the 55 stays inside. Method one is to find the largest perfect-square factor of the radicand and split it off. A radical is called simplified when no perfect-square factor bigger than 11 remains underneath, and 7575​ means 77 times 55​, the usual silent multiplication.
Problem
The factorization is handed to you this time. Use 63=9⋅763=9⋅7 to simplify 6363​ to the form a7a7​. Enter aa.
Show a hint
  • The product rule splits 6363​ across the two factors you were given.
  • 9⋅7=9⋅79⋅7​=9​⋅7​, and one of those two is a whole number.
Show the full solution
63=9 7=3763​=9​7​=3​7​. The perfect-square factor 99 leaves the radical as 33, and the 77 stays inside.
Problem
Simplify 592592​ to abab​ with bb as small as possible. A perfect square bigger than 44 divides 592592. Enter bb.
Show a hint
  • Pulling out the first square you spot is not always the last word. Check what is left under the radical.
  • Splitting off 44 gives 21482148​, and 148148 still has a perfect-square factor.
Show the full solution
592=16⋅37592=16⋅37, so 592=16 37=437592​=16​37​=437​ and b=37b=37​. Stopping at 21482148​ is the common miss. 148=4⋅37148=4⋅37 still has a square factor, so the job was only half done.
Key idea
Prime pairs. The second method never stalls. Factor the radicand into primes. Each pair of the same prime is a perfect square, so a pair leaves the radical as one copy, since p⋅p=pp⋅p​=p, while every unpaired prime stays inside, and the primes that stay multiply back together. This method also proves when you are done. If no prime repeats, nothing can come out, and a radicand with no repeated prime factor is called squarefree. A squarefree radicand is not a radical you failed to simplify. It is one that is already finished.
Problem
Two pairs of the same prime this time. 4941=34⋅614941=34⋅61. Pair the primes to simplify 49414941​ to abab​ with bb as small as possible. Enter aa.
Show a hint
  • 3434 is two separate pairs of 33, and each pair leaves the radical as one copy.
  • The two exited 33s multiply together out front. Only the 6161 stays inside.
Show the full solution
34=32⋅3234=32⋅32 is two pairs, and each pair leaves the radical as a 33, so 4941=3⋅3⋅61=9614941​=3⋅3⋅61​=9​61​. One pair at a time also works, 4941=35494941​=3549​ and 549=9⋅61549=9⋅61, it just takes two steps.
Problem
Not every radical can be simplified. Of 6666​, 8585​, 110110​, and 348348​, how many can be? Enter the count.
Show a hint
  • A radical simplifies exactly when some prime repeats in the radicand's factorization.
  • Factor each radicand and look for a repeated prime. Three of the four have none.
Show the full solution
66=2⋅3⋅1166=2⋅3⋅11, 85=5⋅1785=5⋅17, and 110=2⋅5⋅11110=2⋅5⋅11 have no repeated prime, so those three are already simplified. Only 348=22⋅3⋅29348=22⋅3⋅29 has a pair, giving 287287​, so the count is 11​. A squarefree radicand is not stuck, it is finished.
Key idea
The quotient rule. Division splits the same way. Power of a quotient from 3.1 gives each base its own exponent, so (ab)1/2=a1/2b1/2(ba​)1/2=b1/2a1/2​, which in radical notation is ab=abba​​=b​a​​ for nonnegative aa and positive bb. The move that pays is to reduce the fraction under the radical before rooting anything. A fraction that looks hopeless often reduces to a perfect square over a perfect square, and then the root is a plain fraction with no radical left anywhere.
Problem
Evaluate 490810810490​​ exactly, reducing the fraction under the radical first. Enter the value as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Simplify the fraction before touching the radical.
  • Divide the top and the bottom by 1010. Both results are perfect squares.
Show the full solution
490810=4981810490​=8149​, so 490810=4981=4981=79.810490​​=8149​​=81​49​​=97​​. Rooting first leaves 490490​ over 810810​, and neither is a whole number. Reducing first made both perfect squares.
Problem
Combine 53⋅21253​⋅212​ under one radical. Neither factor alone is a whole number, but the product is. Enter the whole-number value.
Show a hint
  • One radical first, then look for pairs among the prime factors.
  • 212=4⋅53212=4⋅53, so the combined radicand is 4⋅5324⋅532.
Show the full solution
53⋅212=53⋅212=4⋅532=2⋅53=10653​⋅212​=53⋅212​=4⋅532​=2⋅53=106​. Two numbers with no exact decimal form multiplied to a plain whole number, which is why exact forms are worth keeping until the end.
Key idea
Like radicals. Addition obeys a stricter rule. The like-terms idea from 2.4 transfers whole, ab+cb=(a+c)bab​+cb​=(a+c)b​ by the distributive property, exactly as 2x+3x=5x2x+3x=5x. But the product rule has no addition twin. a+ba​+b​ is not a+ba+b​, and radicals only combine under addition when they are like, meaning the same radicand after simplifying. That last clause is the working rule. Unsimplified radicals hide their likeness, so simplify every term first, then compare radicands.
Problem
204+459204​+459​ looks like a sum of unlike radicals. Simplify each term, then enter the coefficient of 5151​ in the sum.
Show a hint
  • Neither term is simplified yet, and likeness only shows after both are.
  • 204=4⋅51204=4⋅51 and 459=9⋅51459=9⋅51.
Show the full solution
204=251204​=251​ and 459=351459​=351​, so the sum is 251+351=551251​+351​=5​51​. The two radicals were like all along. Simplifying is what made it visible.
Problem
Compute 2303−752−4232303​−752​−423​ exactly. No decimals and no estimating. The exact value is a number you can type. Enter it.
Show a hint
  • Three ugly radicals can all be multiples of one small radical. Simplify each term first.
  • Each radicand is a perfect square times 4747.
Show the full solution
2303=49⋅472303=49⋅47, 752=16⋅47752=16⋅47, and 423=9⋅47423=9⋅47, so the expression is 747−447−347=(7−4−3)47=0747​−447​−347​=(7−4−3)47​=0​. The surprise is the point. Simplifying can collapse a whole expression to nothing.
Key idea
Radicals under the old laws. A radical is a fractional power, so every 3.3 move still applies. Powers of radicals collapse through power of a power, (a)4=(a1/2)4=a2(a​)4=(a1/2)4=a2. Cube roots simplify by the same pairing idea, except a prime needs three copies to leave, since p⋅p⋅p3=p3p⋅p⋅p​=p, so hunt for triples instead of pairs. Letter bases work too. For positive yy, y10=(y10)1/2=y5y10​=(y10)1/2=y5, power of a power again, halving the exponent.
Problem
A cube root to close. 344=23⋅43344=23⋅43. Simplify 34433344​ to ab3a3b​ with bb as small as possible. Enter bb.
Show a hint
  • Under a cube root a prime needs three copies to leave, not two.
  • The triple of 22s leaves as a single 22. Count what has no triple.
Show the full solution
The triple of 22s leaves the radical as one 22, so 3443=24333344​=2343​ and b=43b=43​. Pulling out a mere pair of 22s is the square-root habit misfiring, since 44 is not a perfect cube.
Fun fact
The radical sign first appeared in print in 1525, in Christoff Rudolff's algebra book Die Coss, as a bare hook with no bar, likely a hurried letter r for radix, Latin for root. The overbar across the radicand came later. Descartes fused the two into today's symbol in 1637.

Look at what this lesson actually did. Radicals were multiplied, split apart, and added when like. Every division came out clean, because every fraction under a radical reduced to perfect squares. 3.5 faces the division that does not come out clean. Its first answers are correct but awkward to work with, and they get a cleanup rule of their own.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Evaluate 49004900​.
Show the solution
4900=49⋅1004900=49⋅100, so 4900=49 100=7⋅10=704900​=49​100​=7⋅10=70​. The product rule turns one big square root into two easy ones.
Practice
Enter the exact value of (83)2(83​)2.
Show the solution
8383​ is the nonnegative number whose square is 8383, so (83)2=83(83​)2=83​. That is the symbol's whole job. In exponent form, (831/2)2=831(831/2)2=831 says the same thing.
Practice
Exactly one of −512−512​ and −51233−512​ names a real number. Enter its value.
Show the solution
(−8)3=−512(−8)3=−512, so −5123=−83−512​=−8​. No real number squares to −512−512, so −512−512​ names nothing, while an odd root passes a negative sign straight through.
Practice
A student answers −34−34 for 11561156​, and the check (−34)2=1156(−34)2=1156 comes out right. The answer is still wrong. Enter the value of 11561156​.
Show the solution
342=1156342=1156, so 1156=341156​=34​. Both 3434 and −34−34 square to 11561156, and the radical sign names the nonnegative one, the same convention 11561/211561/2 carried in 3.3. The other candidate is written −1156−1156​.
Practice
A student claims that a+b=a+ba​+b​=a+b​. Test the claim the 1.4 way at a=9a=9 and b=16b=16, then enter the true value of 9+169​+16​.
Show the solution
9+16=3+4=79​+16​=3+4=7​. The claim would need 9+16=25=59+16​=25​=5 to equal 77, and it does not. The product rule splits multiplication across a radical, but it has no addition twin.
Practice
Simplify 152152​ to the form a38a38​. Enter aa.
Show the solution
152=4⋅38152=4⋅38, so 152=4 38=238152​=4​38​=2​38​.
Practice
Simplify 142142​ to abab​ with bb as small as possible. Enter bb.
Show the solution
142=2⋅71142=2⋅71 has no repeated prime, so nothing comes out. 142142​ is already 1⋅1421⋅142​, and b=142b=142​. A squarefree radicand means the radical is finished, not that you missed a trick.
Practice
Simplify 585585​ to abab​ with bb as small as possible. Enter the product a⋅ba⋅b, a times b, as a single number.
Show the solution
585=9⋅65585=9⋅65, so 585=365585​=365​, and a⋅b=3⋅65=195a⋅b=3⋅65=195​. Since 65=5⋅1365=5⋅13 has no repeated prime, bb is as small as it can get.
Practice
Evaluate 9615015096​​ exactly. Enter a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
96150=162515096​=2516​, so 96150=1625=4515096​​=25​16​​=54​, 4/54/5​. Rooting 9696 and 150150 separately leaves a mess that the one reduction avoids.
Practice
624−351624​−351​ simplifies all the way down to a single radical bb​. Enter bb.
Show the solution
624=439624​=439​ and 351=339351​=339​, so the difference is 439−339=139439​−339​=139​ and b=39b=39​. Subtracting radicands would give 273273​, which is wrong, since no rule pushes subtraction under a radical.
Practice
For positive yy, y194=yky194​=yk. Enter kk.
Show the solution
y194=(y194)1/2=y194⋅12=y97y194​=(y194)1/2=y194⋅21​=y97, so k=97k=97​. Halving the exponent works whenever the base is positive and the exponent is even.
Practice
Evaluate (46)4(46​)4.
Show the solution
(46)4=(461/2)4=462=2116(46​)4=(461/2)4=462=2116​. Grouping as ((46)2)2=462((46​)2)2=462 says the same thing without exponent notation.
Practice
Combine 657⋅146657​⋅146​ under one radical, then simplify to abab​ with bb as small as possible. Enter aa.
Show the solution
657⋅146=32⋅732⋅2657⋅146=32⋅732⋅2, so 657 146=3⋅73⋅2=2192657​146​=3⋅73⋅2​=219​2​. Multiplying out to 9592295922 first also works, but the pairs are easier to see before the multiplication buries them.
Practice
Evaluate 126686686126​​ exactly. Enter a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
126686=949686126​=499​, so the root is 949=3749​9​​=73​, 3/73/7​. Neither 126126 nor 686686 is a perfect square on its own, and the single reduction is what makes both layers come out clean.
Practice
Simplify 47233472​ to ab3a3b​ with bb as small as possible. Enter bb.
Show the solution
472=23⋅59472=23⋅59, and the triple of 22s exits as one 22, so 4723=25933472​=2359​ and b=59b=59​. Writing 2118323118​ from 472=4⋅118472=4⋅118 is the square-root habit misfiring, since a pair of 22s does nothing under a cube root.
Practice
Factor 50565056 into primes to simplify 50565056​ to abab​ with bb as small as possible. Enter the product a⋅ba⋅b, a times b, as a single number.
Show the solution
5056=26⋅795056=26⋅79. The three pairs of 22s leave as 2⋅2⋅2=82⋅2⋅2=8 and the unpaired 7979 stays, so 5056=8795056​=879​ and a⋅b=8⋅79=632a⋅b=8⋅79=632​. Stopping early at 43164316​ or 2126421264​ leaves a square inside, and bb is only as small as possible once no prime repeats.
Practice
Simplify 335⋅737335​⋅737​ to abab​ with bb as small as possible. Enter the sum a+ba+b, a plus b, as a single number.
Show the solution
335⋅737=5⋅67⋅11⋅67=672⋅55335⋅737=5⋅67⋅11⋅67=672⋅55, so 335 737=6755335​737​=6755​, and a+b=67+55=122a+b=67+55=122​. The shared 6767 is invisible until both radicands sit under one radical, which is why combining comes first.
